name: Work, Learn and Grow (WLG)
org: NYC Council initiative, run by youth groups such as the Police Athletic League and Henry Street Settlement
what_you_do: Keep working during the school year after your summer SYEP job. You get career training and a paid entry-level job at a place like a hospital, museum, city agency, law firm or store.
who_can_apply: Youth ages 14 to 24 who were in the prior Summer Youth Employment Program (SYEP) cycle and are enrolled in school now.
pay_detail: Paid employment. The pages do not state a rate.
duration: Up to 25 weeks between October and April (PAL). Henry Street says its program runs November to March.
deadline_text: Henry Street says applications are typically released in late September. No 2026 to 2027 deadline is posted on either page.
how_to_apply: Apply through an SYEP provider that runs WLG. Eligible applicants are entered into a lottery. Contact PAL (Myshanda Parks, MParks@palnyc.org) or Henry Street (Iliana Balbuena, ibalbuena@henrystreet.org).
notes: Only for teens who did SYEP last summer. If you are new, start with the Summer Youth Employment Program. Selection is by lottery, so a spot is not guaranteed. New York State requires working papers for workers ages 14 to 17.
